intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 (CLCRP2) is caused by compound heterozygous mutation in the SEC24D gene.

checks.explanation: Compound heterozygous SEC24D mutations cause the phenotype. The boy's features most closely resembled Cole-Carpenter syndrome; the CLCRP2 label is OMIM naming.

paragraphs.text: Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 is a skeletal disorder with bone fragility. Features include severely disturbed ossification of the skull, multiple fractures that may begin before birth, short stature, and craniofacial malformations such as macrocephaly, frontal bossing, midface hypoplasia, and micrognathia (Garbes et al., 2015; Takeyari et al., 2018). Some patients with SEC24D mutations have been reported as having autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta (Zhang et al., 2017).

paragraphs.text: Garbes et al. (2015) reported 3 affected individuals from 2 families: a 7-year-old boy whose phenotype most closely resembled Cole-Carpenter syndrome, and 2 fetuses initially suspected to have a severe type of osteogenesis imperfecta. All 3 had severely disturbed ossification of the skull and multiple fractures with prenatal onset. The boy had short stature and craniofacial malformations including macrocephaly, midface hypoplasia, micrognathia, frontal bossing, and downslanting palpebral fissures.

paragraphs.text: Zhang et al. (2017) reported 2 Chinese probands with autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta. The proband in family 1, a 23-year-old man, had recurrent fractures, dentinogenesis imperfecta, an unclosed anterior fontanel, and facial dysmorphism. CT 3-dimensional imaging of the cranium showed skull deformities with a broad ossification defect in the frontoapical area, a widened sagittal suture, and wormian bones. The proband in family 2, a 7-year-old boy, also had recurrent fractures, dentinogenesis imperfecta, and an unclosed anterior fontanel, but no obvious facial dysmorphism.

paragraphs.text: By whole-exome sequencing, Garbes et al. (2015) identified compound heterozygous mutations in the SEC24D gene in 3 individuals from 2 families with a similar skeletal phenotype. Three mutant alleles were found: a truncating mutation, c.613C-T (Q205X), and 2 missense mutations, c.3044C-T (S1015F), located in a cargo-binding pocket, and c.2933A-C (Q978P), located in the gelsolin-like domain. Each affected individual carried 2 of these alleles; c.3044C-T was found in all 3 and lay within a 14-Mb founder haplotype that they shared. Electron and immunofluorescence microscopy of the boy's skin fibroblasts showed inefficient ER export of procollagen and dilated ER tubules. This matched the cellular phenotype of individuals with cranio-lentico-sutural dysplasia, which is caused by SEC23A mutations.
